pt.title: [Varejo 101 #11] Por Que Um Canto Imprime Dinheiro e o Próximo Quarteirão Fica Escuro

segments.src: > Retail real estate isn't about finding a "good spot" — it's about matching a specific store format to the specific pool of people who can realistically reach it.
segments.tr: > Imóveis de varejo não se trata de encontrar um "bom local" — é sobre combinar um formato de loja específico com o grupo específico de pessoas que podem realisticamente alcançá-lo.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: There's an old line in retail: the three things that matter are location, location, and location.
segments.tr: Há uma velha máxima no varejo: as três coisas que importam são local, local e local.

segments.src: It's a cliché, but it survives because store location is one of the few decisions you can't undo cheaply.
segments.tr: É um clichê, mas persiste porque a localização da loja é uma das poucas decisões que você não pode desfazer barato.

segments.src: You can re-merchandise a shelf on Tuesday.
segments.tr: Você pode reorganizar a mercadoria de uma prateleira na terça-feira.

segments.src: You can drop prices tonight.
segments.tr: Você pode reduzir os preços hoje à noite.

segments.src: You cannot move a 30,000-square-foot building with a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: Você não pode mover um edifício de 30 mil pés quadrados com um contrato de 15 anos.

segments.src: Location strategy breaks into three questions that get asked in order.
segments.tr: A estratégia de localização se divide em três perguntas que são feitas em ordem.

segments.src: What factors make a site work?** Retailers evaluate sites on a handful of measurable things:
segments.tr: Quais fatores tornam um local viável?** Os varejistas avaliam os locais em um punhado de coisas mensuráveis:

segments.src: - **Traffic** — vehicle counts (published by state DOTs as annual average daily traffic, or AADT) and foot traffic. But raw volume isn't enough. Cars doing 55 mph past a median-divided highway can't turn left into your parking lot.
segments.tr: - **Tráfego** — contagens de veículos (publicadas pelos DOTs estaduais como tráfego médio diário anual, ou AADT) e tráfego de pedestres. Mas o volume bruto não é suficiente. Carros viajando a 55 mph em uma rodovia com divisória mediana não conseguem virar à esquerda para seu estacionamento.

segments.src: - **Accessibility** — curb cuts, signal lights, left-turn access, parking ratio (commonly around 4–5 spaces per 1,000 sq ft for shopping centers), and how easy it is to get *out* as well as in.
segments.tr: - **Acessibilidade** — cortes de meio-fio, semáforos, acesso com conversão à esquerda, relação de estacionamento (comumente cerca de 4–5 espaços por 1.000 pés quadrados para centros comerciais), e como é fácil sair e entrar.

segments.src: - **Visibility** — sightlines from the road, signage rights, and how far ahead a driver can spot you.
segments.tr: - **Visibilidade** — linhas de visão da estrada, direitos de sinalização, e a que distância um motorista pode vê-lo.

segments.src: - **Trade area demographics** — population, household income, age mix, and daytime population (the workers who show up 9-to-5 but sleep elsewhere).
segments.tr: - **Demografia da área de atuação** — população, renda familiar, composição etária e população diurna (os trabalhadores que aparecem das 9 às 17 horas, mas dormem em outro lugar).

segments.src: - **Competition and co-tenancy** — nearby stores that steal your customers versus ones that deliver them. A nail salon wants to be next to a grocery anchor. A furniture store is happy next to another furniture store, because shoppers comparison-shop big-ticket items.
segments.tr: - **Concorrência e co-ocupação** — lojas próximas que roubam seus clientes versus aquelas que os trazem. Um salão de unhas quer ficar ao lado de uma âncora de supermercado. Uma loja de móveis fica feliz ao lado de outra loja de móveis, porque os compradores fazem comparações em itens de alto valor.

segments.src: - **Cost and terms** — base rent per square foot per year, CAM (common area maintenance) charges, percentage rent, lease length, and any exclusivity or co-tenancy clauses.
segments.tr: - **Custo e termos** — aluguel base por pé quadrado por ano, cobranças de CAM (manutenção de área comum), aluguel percentual, prazo do contrato, e quaisquer cláusulas de exclusividade ou co-ocupação.

segments.src: Who can actually reach it?** That's **trade area analysis**.
segments.tr: Quem realmente pode alcançá-lo?** Essa é a **análise da área de atuação**.

segments.src: A trade area is the geographic zone a store draws customers from, usually split into three rings:
segments.tr: Uma área de atuação é a zona geográfica da qual uma loja atrai clientes, geralmente dividida em três anéis:

segments.src: - **Primary** — roughly 50–70% of customers, closest in
segments.tr: - **Primária** — aproximadamente 50–70% dos clientes, os mais próximos

segments.src: - **Secondary** — the next 20–30%
segments.tr: - **Secundária** — os próximos 20–30%

segments.src: - **Tertiary** — the scattered remainder, including people passing through
segments.tr: - **Terciária** — o restante disperso, incluindo pessoas passando

segments.src: Practitioners rarely draw simple circles anymore.
segments.tr: Os profissionais raramente desenham círculos simples nos dias atuais.

segments.src: They use **drive-time polygons** (a 5-, 10-, and 15-minute drive radius, which bends around rivers, highways, and dead ends) and, increasingly, anonymized mobile-location data showing where customers actually came from.
segments.tr: Eles usam **polígonos de tempo de viagem** (um raio de 5, 10 e 15 minutos de viagem, que se curva em torno de rios, rodovias e becos sem saída) e, cada vez mais, dados anonimizados de localização móvel mostrando de onde os clientes realmente vieram.

segments.src: The classic analytical tool is the **gravity model**.
segments.tr: A ferramenta analítica clássica é o **modelo de gravitação**.

segments.src: The intuition is borrowed from physics: a store's pull grows with its size and shrinks with the distance (or travel time) shoppers must cover.
segments.tr: A intuição é emprestada da física: o alcance de uma loja cresce com seu tamanho e encolhe com a distância (ou tempo de viagem) que os compradores devem percorrer.

segments.src: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k
segments.tr: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k

segments.src: The Huff model formalizes this — it estimates the *probability* a given household shops at Store A rather than Store B, which is more useful than a hard boundary line, because real trade areas are fuzzy and overlapping.
segments.tr: O modelo Huff formaliza isso — ele estima a *probabilidade* de uma determinada casa comprar na Loja A em vez da Loja B, o que é mais útil do que uma linha de limite rígido, porque as áreas de atuação reais são difusas e sobrepostas.

segments.src: A related check is **cannibalization**: if your new store's trade area overlaps an existing one you already own, part of your "new" sales is just sales moving across town.
segments.tr: Uma verificação relacionada é **canibalização**: se a área de atuação da sua nova loja se sobrepõe a uma existente que você já possui, parte de suas vendas "novas" é apenas vendas movendo-se pela cidade.

segments.src: What kind of site is it?** Location types come with built-in trade-offs:
segments.tr: Que tipo de local é?** Os tipos de localização vêm com compensações intrínsecas:

segments.src: - **Unplanned / freestanding** — a standalone building, often a pad or outparcel at the edge of a shopping center lot. Cheap per square foot, great parking, full signage control, but no neighbor pulling traffic for you. Works for destination brands (Walgreens, a drive-thru quick-service restaurant).
segments.tr: - **Não planejado / isolado** — um edifício independente, geralmente um lote ou parcela fora do centro comercial. Barato por pé quadrado, ótimo estacionamento, controle total de sinalização, mas nenhum vizinho atraindo tráfego para você. Funciona para marcas de destino (Walgreens, um restaurante de serviço rápido com drive-thru).

segments.src: - **Central business district (CBD)** — downtown. High daytime population, high rent, limited parking, weekend traffic that can fall off a cliff in office-heavy districts.
segments.tr: - **Distrito comercial central (CBD)** — centro da cidade. Alta população diurna, aluguel alto, estacionamento limitado, tráfego de fim de semana que pode cair drasticamente em distritos pesados em escritórios.

segments.src: - **Strip / neighborhood center** — a line of stores with surface parking, usually anchored by a supermarket or a drugstore. Built for convenience and errand trips.
segments.tr: - **Centro de faixa / vizinhança** — uma fileira de lojas com estacionamento na superfície, geralmente ancorada por um supermercado ou farmácia. Construído para conveniência e viagens de recados.

segments.src: - **Power center** — a cluster of big-box category killers (home improvement, pet supply, off-price apparel). Draws from a wide radius.
segments.tr: - **Centro de poder** — um aglomerado de grandes lojas de categoria (melhoria do lar, suprimentos para animais de estimação, roupas com desconto). Atrai de um raio amplo.

segments.src: - **Enclosed regional mall** — big trade area, high traffic, high rent, strict operating rules and long leases.
segments.tr: - **Shopping center regional fechado** — grande área de atuação, alto tráfego, aluguel alto, regras operacionais rigorosas e contratos longos.

segments.src: - **Lifestyle center** — open-air, upscale, restaurant-heavy; sells atmosphere and dwell time.
segments.tr: - **Centro de estilo de vida** — ao ar livre, sofisticado, pesado em restaurantes; vende atmosfera e tempo de permanência.

segments.src: - **Airports, campuses, transit hubs** — captive audiences, premium pricing, brutal rent and operating restrictions.
segments.tr: - **Aeroportos, campi, centros de trânsito** — públicos cativos, preços premium, aluguel brutal e restrições operacionais.

segments.src: The right answer depends entirely on format.
segments.tr: A resposta certa depende inteiramente do formato.

segments.src: A convenience store needs a right-turn-in on the evening commute side of the road.
segments.tr: Uma loja de conveniência precisa de um acesso com conversão à direita no lado da rua do trajeto da tarde.

segments.src: A destination retailer like IKEA can sit by a highway interchange 25 minutes away and still fill the lot, because people plan the trip.
segments.tr: Um varejista de destino como IKEA pode ficar perto de uma troca de rodovia 25 minutos de distância e ainda assim encher o estacionamento, porque as pessoas planejam a viagem.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks and a Costco in the same American suburb.
segments.tr: Pense em um Starbucks e um Costco no mesmo subúrbio americano.

segments.src: The Starbucks sits on the *morning* side of a busy arterial — the inbound-commute side — with a right-turn-in entrance and a drive-thru wrapping the building.
segments.tr: O Starbucks fica no lado *matinal* de uma artéria movimentada — o lado do trajeto de entrada — com uma entrada com conversão à direita e um drive-thru contornando o edifício.

segments.src: Its primary trade area may be only a mile or two wide.
segments.tr: Sua área de atuação primária pode ter apenas uma ou duas milhas de largura.

segments.src: Nobody plans a 20-minute drive for a latte, so it lives on interception: catching a trip already in progress.
segments.tr: Ninguém planeja uma viagem de 20 minutos para um latte, então ela sobrevive da interceptação: pegando uma viagem já em andamento.

segments.src: That's why you'll see two Starbucks locations facing each other across the same road.
segments.tr: É por isso que você verá dois locais de Starbucks em lados opostos da mesma rua.

segments.src: They're not competing so much as covering opposite commute directions, and the company accepts a bit of cannibalization to own both flows.
segments.tr: Eles não estão competindo tanto quanto cobrindo direções de trajeto opostas, e a empresa aceita um pouco de canibalização para dominar ambos os fluxos.

segments.src: Costco plays the opposite game.
segments.tr: Costco joga o jogo oposto.

segments.src: There's one per region, usually near a freeway interchange with a huge lot and a gas station out front.
segments.tr: Há um por região, geralmente perto de uma troca de rodovia com um lote enorme e um posto de gasolina na frente.

segments.src: People will drive 25 minutes and load a cart with $250 of goods.
segments.tr: As pessoas dirigirão 25 minutos e carregarão um carrinho com $250 em mercadorias.

segments.src: Its trade area is measured in a 15-minute-plus drive time, not blocks.
segments.tr: Sua área de atuação é medida em um tempo de viagem de 15 minutos ou mais, não em quarteirões.

segments.src: The gravity model explains both: Costco's enormous size overcomes distance decay, while Starbucks' small size means it must live very close to its customer.
segments.tr: O modelo de gravitação explica ambos: o tamanho enorme do Costco supera o decaimento de distância, enquanto o pequeno tamanho do Starbucks significa que ele deve ficar muito perto de seus clientes.

segments.src: Now look at the strip mall nearby.
segments.tr: Agora olhe para o shopping de faixa próximo.

segments.src: The grocery anchor probably pays $8–$15 per square foot in annual base rent, while the small inline shops next to it might pay $30–$45, plus $5–$10 in CAM.
segments.tr: A âncora de supermercado provavelmente paga $8–$15 por pé quadrado em aluguel base anual, enquanto as pequenas lojas incorporadas ao lado podem pagar $30–$45, mais $5–$10 em CAM.

segments.src: The anchor pays less because it *generates* the traffic everyone else feeds on.
segments.tr: A âncora paga menos porque *gera* o tráfego do qual todos os outros se alimentam.

segments.src: And many small-shop leases include a **co-tenancy clause**: if the anchor goes dark, the small tenant can cut rent or walk.
segments.tr: E muitos contratos de pequenas lojas incluem uma **cláusula de co-ocupação**: se a âncora fecha, o pequeno inquilino pode reduzir o aluguel ou sair.

segments.src: That clause exists precisely because their location value came from the neighbor, not the address.
segments.tr: Essa cláusula existe precisamente porque seu valor de localização veio do vizinho, não do endereço.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. Site selection weighs traffic, accessibility, visibility, trade-area demographics, competition and co-tenancy, and total occupancy cost — not just rent.
segments.tr: 1. A seleção do local considera tráfego, acessibilidade, visibilidade, demografia da área de atuação, concorrência e co-ocupação, e custo total de ocupação — não apenas aluguel.

segments.src: 2. Trade area analysis defines who can realistically reach a store, using drive-time zones and gravity/Huff models that trade hard boundaries for probabilities, while watching for cannibalization of your own stores.
segments.tr: 2. A análise da área de atuação define quem pode realisticamente alcançar uma loja, usando zonas de tempo de viagem e modelos de gravitação/Huff que trocam limites rígidos por probabilidades, enquanto observam a canibalização de suas próprias lojas.

segments.src: 3. Location type — freestanding, CBD, strip center, power center, mall, lifestyle center, or captive venue — must match the store's format, because convenience retailers intercept trips while destination retailers can pull people across a whole metro.
segments.tr: 3. O tipo de localização — isolado, CBD, centro de faixa, centro de poder, shopping, centro de estilo de vida ou local cativo — deve corresponder ao formato da loja, porque varejistas de conveniência interceptam viagens enquanto varejistas de destino podem atrair pessoas em toda uma metrópole.

segments.tr: **Q2 — F (falso).** A âncora geralmente paga o aluguel *mais baixo* por pé quadrado no centro, porque seu papel é gerar o tráfego do qual os inquilinos incorporados dependem; essas pequenas lojas pagam um prêmio por esse transbordamento.

segments.src: **Q3 — (c) Cannibalization.** When trade areas overlap, part of the new store's revenue is transferred from an existing location rather than newly created — which is why site analysis models net incremental sales, not just gross sales at the new site.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — (c) Canibalização.** Quando as áreas de atuação se sobrepõem, parte da receita da nova loja é transferida de um local existente em vez de ser recém-criada — é por isso que os modelos de análise do local modelam vendas incrementais líquidas, não apenas vendas brutas no novo local.*

in.title: [Ritel 101 #11] Mengapa Satu Sudut Menguntungkan Sedangkan Blok Berikutnya Sepi

segments.src: > Retail real estate isn't about finding a "good spot" — it's about matching a specific store format to the specific pool of people who can realistically reach it.
segments.tr: > Aset real estat ritel bukan tentang menemukan "tempat yang bagus" — tetapi tentang mencocokkan format toko tertentu dengan pool spesifik orang yang dapat secara realistis menjangkaunya.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: There's an old line in retail: the three things that matter are location, location, and location.
segments.tr: Ada pepatah lama dalam ritel: tiga hal yang penting adalah lokasi, lokasi, dan lokasi.

segments.src: It's a cliché, but it survives because store location is one of the few decisions you can't undo cheaply.
segments.tr: Ini adalah klise, tetapi bertahan karena lokasi toko adalah salah satu dari sedikit keputusan yang tidak bisa dibatalkan dengan murah.

segments.src: You can re-merchandise a shelf on Tuesday.
segments.tr: Anda dapat mengatur ulang barang di rak pada hari Selasa.

segments.src: You can drop prices tonight.
segments.tr: Anda dapat menurunkan harga malam ini.

segments.src: You cannot move a 30,000-square-foot building with a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: Anda tidak dapat memindahkan bangunan 30.000 kaki persegi dengan sewa 15 tahun.

segments.src: Location strategy breaks into three questions that get asked in order.
segments.tr: Strategi lokasi terbagi menjadi tiga pertanyaan yang diajukan secara berurutan.

segments.src: What factors make a site work?** Retailers evaluate sites on a handful of measurable things:
segments.tr: Faktor apa yang membuat situs berfungsi?** Pengecer mengevaluasi situs berdasarkan beberapa hal yang dapat diukur:

segments.src: - **Traffic** — vehicle counts (published by state DOTs as annual average daily traffic, or AADT) and foot traffic. But raw volume isn't enough. Cars doing 55 mph past a median-divided highway can't turn left into your parking lot.
segments.tr: - **Lalu lintas** — perhitungan kendaraan (dipublikasikan oleh DOT negara bagian sebagai lalu lintas harian rata-rata tahunan, atau AADT) dan lalu lintas pejalan kaki. Tetapi volume mentah tidak cukup. Mobil yang melaju 55 mph melewati jalan raya yang terbagi median tidak dapat berbelok kiri ke tempat parkir Anda.

segments.src: - **Accessibility** — curb cuts, signal lights, left-turn access, parking ratio (commonly around 4–5 spaces per 1,000 sq ft for shopping centers), and how easy it is to get *out* as well as in.
segments.tr: - **Aksesibilitas** — potongan tepi jalan, lampu sinyal, akses belok kiri, rasio parkir (biasanya sekitar 4–5 tempat per 1.000 kaki persegi untuk pusat perbelanjaan), dan seberapa mudah untuk keluar serta masuk.

segments.src: - **Visibility** — sightlines from the road, signage rights, and how far ahead a driver can spot you.
segments.tr: - **Visibilitas** — garis pandang dari jalan, hak tanda, dan seberapa jauh ke depan seorang pengemudi dapat melihat Anda.

segments.src: - **Trade area demographics** — population, household income, age mix, and daytime population (the workers who show up 9-to-5 but sleep elsewhere).
segments.tr: - **Demografi area perdagangan** — populasi, pendapatan rumah tangga, campuran usia, dan populasi siang hari (pekerja yang muncul pukul 9 hingga 5 tetapi tidur di tempat lain).

segments.src: - **Competition and co-tenancy** — nearby stores that steal your customers versus ones that deliver them. A nail salon wants to be next to a grocery anchor. A furniture store is happy next to another furniture store, because shoppers comparison-shop big-ticket items.
segments.tr: - **Kompetisi dan co-tenancy** — toko terdekat yang mencuri pelanggan Anda versus yang memberikan mereka. Salon kuku ingin berada di sebelah jangkar bahan makanan. Toko furnitur senang berada di sebelah toko furnitur lain, karena pembeli membandingkan-belanja barang bernilai tinggi.

segments.src: - **Cost and terms** — base rent per square foot per year, CAM (common area maintenance) charges, percentage rent, lease length, and any exclusivity or co-tenancy clauses.
segments.tr: - **Biaya dan syarat** — sewa dasar per kaki persegi per tahun, biaya CAM (pemeliharaan area bersama), persentase sewa, jangka waktu sewa, dan klausul eksklusivitas atau co-tenancy apa pun.

segments.src: Who can actually reach it?** That's **trade area analysis**.
segments.tr: Siapa yang benar-benar dapat menjangkaunya?** Itu adalah **analisis area perdagangan**.

segments.src: A trade area is the geographic zone a store draws customers from, usually split into three rings:
segments.tr: Wilayah perdagangan adalah zona geografis tempat toko menarik pelanggan, biasanya dibagi menjadi tiga cincin:

segments.src: - **Primary** — roughly 50–70% of customers, closest in
segments.tr: - **Utama** — kira-kira 50–70% pelanggan, paling dekat

segments.src: - **Secondary** — the next 20–30%
segments.tr: - **Sekunder** — 20–30% berikutnya

segments.src: - **Tertiary** — the scattered remainder, including people passing through
segments.tr: - **Tersier** — sisanya yang tersebar, termasuk orang yang melewati

segments.src: Practitioners rarely draw simple circles anymore.
segments.tr: Praktisi jarang menggambar lingkaran sederhana lagi.

segments.src: They use **drive-time polygons** (a 5-, 10-, and 15-minute drive radius, which bends around rivers, highways, and dead ends) and, increasingly, anonymized mobile-location data showing where customers actually came from.
segments.tr: Mereka menggunakan **poligon waktu-berkendara** (radius berkendara 5, 10, dan 15 menit, yang membengkok di sekitar sungai, jalan raya, dan jalan buntu) dan, semakin banyak, data lokasi seluler yang anonim menunjukkan dari mana pelanggan sebenarnya berasal.

segments.src: The classic analytical tool is the **gravity model**.
segments.tr: Alat analitik klasik adalah **model gravitasi**.

segments.src: The intuition is borrowed from physics: a store's pull grows with its size and shrinks with the distance (or travel time) shoppers must cover.
segments.tr: Intuisinya dipinjam dari fisika: tarikan toko tumbuh dengan ukurannya dan menyusut dengan jarak (atau waktu perjalanan) yang harus ditempuh pembeli.

segments.src: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k
segments.tr: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k

segments.src: The Huff model formalizes this — it estimates the *probability* a given household shops at Store A rather than Store B, which is more useful than a hard boundary line, because real trade areas are fuzzy and overlapping.
segments.tr: Model Huff memformalkan ini — ia memperkirakan *kemungkinan* rumah tangga tertentu berbelanja di Toko A daripada Toko B, yang lebih berguna daripada garis batas keras, karena wilayah perdagangan nyata kabur dan tumpang tindih.

segments.src: A related check is **cannibalization**: if your new store's trade area overlaps an existing one you already own, part of your "new" sales is just sales moving across town.
segments.tr: Pemeriksaan terkait adalah **kanibalisme**: jika wilayah perdagangan toko baru Anda tumpang tindih dengan yang sudah ada yang sudah Anda miliki, bagian dari penjualan "baru" Anda hanyalah penjualan yang berpindah ke seberang kota.

segments.src: What kind of site is it?** Location types come with built-in trade-offs:
segments.tr: Jenis situs apa itu?** Jenis lokasi dilengkapi dengan pertukaran bawaan:

segments.src: - **Unplanned / freestanding** — a standalone building, often a pad or outparcel at the edge of a shopping center lot. Cheap per square foot, great parking, full signage control, but no neighbor pulling traffic for you. Works for destination brands (Walgreens, a drive-thru quick-service restaurant).
segments.tr: - **Tidak direncanakan / berdiri sendiri** — bangunan mandiri, sering berupa bantalan atau gundukan di tepi lot pusat perbelanjaan. Murah per kaki persegi, parkir bagus, kontrol tanda penuh, tetapi tidak ada tetangga yang menarik lalu lintas untuk Anda. Bekerja untuk merek destinasi (Walgreens, restoran layanan cepat drive-thru).

segments.src: - **Central business district (CBD)** — downtown. High daytime population, high rent, limited parking, weekend traffic that can fall off a cliff in office-heavy districts.
segments.tr: - **Distrik bisnis pusat (CBD)** — pusat kota. Populasi siang hari tinggi, sewa tinggi, parkir terbatas, lalu lintas akhir pekan yang dapat jatuh dari tebing di distrik berat perkantoran.

segments.src: - **Strip / neighborhood center** — a line of stores with surface parking, usually anchored by a supermarket or a drugstore. Built for convenience and errand trips.
segments.tr: - **Jalur / pusat lingkungan** — serangkaian toko dengan parkir permukaan, biasanya dijangkar oleh supermarket atau apotek. Dibangun untuk kenyamanan dan perjalanan kesalahan.

segments.src: - **Power center** — a cluster of big-box category killers (home improvement, pet supply, off-price apparel). Draws from a wide radius.
segments.tr: - **Pusat kekuatan** — sekelompok pembunuh kategori kotak besar (perbaikan rumah, pasokan hewan peliharaan, pakaian harga miring). Menarik dari radius yang luas.

segments.src: - **Enclosed regional mall** — big trade area, high traffic, high rent, strict operating rules and long leases.
segments.tr: - **Mal regional tertutup** — area perdagangan besar, lalu lintas tinggi, sewa tinggi, aturan operasi ketat dan sewa panjang.

segments.src: - **Lifestyle center** — open-air, upscale, restaurant-heavy; sells atmosphere and dwell time.
segments.tr: - **Pusat gaya hidup** — terbuka, mewah, berat restoran; menjual suasana dan waktu tinggal.

segments.src: - **Airports, campuses, transit hubs** — captive audiences, premium pricing, brutal rent and operating restrictions.
segments.tr: - **Bandara, kampus, pusat transit** — penonton tawanan, harga premium, sewa brutal dan pembatasan operasi.

segments.src: The right answer depends entirely on format.
segments.tr: Jawaban yang tepat tergantung sepenuhnya pada format.

segments.src: A convenience store needs a right-turn-in on the evening commute side of the road.
segments.tr: Toko kelontong memerlukan belok-kanan di sisi perjalanan sore jalan.

segments.src: A destination retailer like IKEA can sit by a highway interchange 25 minutes away and still fill the lot, because people plan the trip.
segments.tr: Pengecer destinasi seperti IKEA dapat duduk di samping simpul jalan raya 25 menit jauhnya dan masih mengisi lotnya, karena orang merencanakan perjalanan.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks and a Costco in the same American suburb.
segments.tr: Pikirkan tentang Starbucks dan Costco di pinggiran kota Amerika yang sama.

segments.src: The Starbucks sits on the *morning* side of a busy arterial — the inbound-commute side — with a right-turn-in entrance and a drive-thru wrapping the building.
segments.tr: Starbucks duduk di sisi *pagi* arteri yang sibuk — sisi perjalanan masuk — dengan pintu masuk belok-kanan dan drive-thru yang membungkus bangunan.

segments.src: Its primary trade area may be only a mile or two wide.
segments.tr: Wilayah perdagangan utamanya mungkin hanya satu atau dua mil lebar.

segments.src: Nobody plans a 20-minute drive for a latte, so it lives on interception: catching a trip already in progress.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang merencanakan perjalanan 20 menit untuk latte, jadi ia hidup pada penyadapan: menangkap perjalanan yang sedang berlangsung.

segments.src: That's why you'll see two Starbucks locations facing each other across the same road.
segments.tr: Itu sebabnya Anda akan melihat dua lokasi Starbucks saling berhadapan di seberang jalan yang sama.

segments.src: They're not competing so much as covering opposite commute directions, and the company accepts a bit of cannibalization to own both flows.
segments.tr: Mereka tidak bersaing banyak karena menutupi arah perjalanan yang berlawanan, dan perusahaan menerima sedikit kanibalisme untuk memiliki kedua aliran.

segments.src: Costco plays the opposite game.
segments.tr: Costco bermain permainan yang berlawanan.

segments.src: There's one per region, usually near a freeway interchange with a huge lot and a gas station out front.
segments.tr: Ada satu per wilayah, biasanya di dekat simpul jalan bebas hambatan dengan banyak besar dan stasiun gas di depan.

segments.src: People will drive 25 minutes and load a cart with $250 of goods.
segments.tr: Orang akan berkendara 25 menit dan memuat keranjang dengan barang senilai $250.

segments.src: Its trade area is measured in a 15-minute-plus drive time, not blocks.
segments.tr: Wilayah perdagangannya diukur dalam waktu berkendara 15 menit atau lebih, bukan blok.

segments.src: The gravity model explains both: Costco's enormous size overcomes distance decay, while Starbucks' small size means it must live very close to its customer.
segments.tr: Model gravitasi menjelaskan keduanya: ukuran Costco yang sangat besar mengatasi penurunan jarak, sementara ukuran kecil Starbucks berarti harus tinggal sangat dekat dengan pelanggannya.

segments.src: Now look at the strip mall nearby.
segments.tr: Sekarang lihat mal jalur di dekatnya.

segments.src: The grocery anchor probably pays $8–$15 per square foot in annual base rent, while the small inline shops next to it might pay $30–$45, plus $5–$10 in CAM.
segments.tr: Jangkar bahan makanan mungkin membayar $8–$15 per kaki persegi dalam sewa dasar tahunan, sementara toko inline kecil di sebelahnya mungkin membayar $30–$45, ditambah $5–$10 dalam CAM.

segments.src: The anchor pays less because it *generates* the traffic everyone else feeds on.
segments.tr: Jangkar membayar lebih sedikit karena ia *menghasilkan* lalu lintas yang semua orang lain berikan.

segments.src: And many small-shop leases include a **co-tenancy clause**: if the anchor goes dark, the small tenant can cut rent or walk.
segments.tr: Dan banyak sewa toko kecil mencakup **klausul co-tenancy**: jika jangkar menjadi gelap, penyewa kecil dapat memotong sewa atau pergi.

segments.src: That clause exists precisely because their location value came from the neighbor, not the address.
segments.tr: Klausul itu ada justru karena nilai lokasi mereka berasal dari tetangga, bukan alamat.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Site selection weighs traffic, accessibility, visibility, trade-area demographics, competition and co-tenancy, and total occupancy cost — not just rent.
segments.tr: 1. Pemilihan situs mempertimbangkan lalu lintas, aksesibilitas, visibilitas, demografi area perdagangan, kompetisi dan co-tenancy, dan biaya okupansi total — bukan hanya sewa.

segments.src: 2. Trade area analysis defines who can realistically reach a store, using drive-time zones and gravity/Huff models that trade hard boundaries for probabilities, while watching for cannibalization of your own stores.
segments.tr: 2. Analisis area perdagangan mendefinisikan siapa yang dapat secara realistis menjangkau toko, menggunakan zona waktu berkendara dan model gravitasi/Huff yang menukar batas keras dengan probabilitas, sambil mengawasi kanibalisme toko Anda sendiri.

segments.src: 3. Location type — freestanding, CBD, strip center, power center, mall, lifestyle center, or captive venue — must match the store's format, because convenience retailers intercept trips while destination retailers can pull people across a whole metro.
segments.tr: 3. Jenis lokasi — berdiri sendiri, CBD, pusat jalur, pusat daya, mal, pusat gaya hidup, atau tempat tawanan — harus sesuai dengan format toko, karena pengecer kenyamanan menyadap perjalanan sementara pengecer destinasi dapat menarik orang di seluruh metro.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **Q1.** In a gravity model of retail attraction, what happens to a store's pull as travel time increases, holding store size constant?
segments.tr: **Q1.** Dalam model gravitasi daya tarik ritel, apa yang terjadi pada tarikan toko saat waktu perjalanan meningkat, dengan ukuran toko tetap konstan?

segments.src: - (a) It increases
segments.tr: - (a) Meningkat

segments.src: - (b) It decreases
segments.tr: - (b) Menurun

segments.src: - (c) It stays the same
segments.tr: - (c) Tetap sama

segments.src: - (d) It depends entirely on rent
segments.tr: - (d) Tergantung sepenuhnya pada sewa

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — In a typical neighborhood shopping center, the grocery anchor usually pays a *higher* base rent per square foot than the small inline shops beside it.
segments.tr: **Q2.** O/X — Dalam pusat perbelanjaan lingkungan khas, jangkar bahan makanan biasanya membayar sewa dasar *lebih tinggi* per kaki persegi daripada toko inline kecil di sebelahnya.

segments.src: **Q3.** A retailer opens a second store four miles from its existing one and total company sales rise far less than the new store's own sales.
segments.tr: **Q3.** Pengecer membuka toko kedua empat mil dari yang sudah ada dan total penjualan perusahaan naik jauh lebih sedikit daripada penjualan toko baru itu sendiri.

segments.src: What is this most likely called?
segments.tr: Apa yang paling mungkin disebut ini?

segments.src: - (a) Co-tenancy
segments.tr: - (a) Co-tenancy

segments.src: - (b) Percentage rent
segments.tr: - (b) Persentase sewa

segments.src: - (c) Cannibalization
segments.tr: - (c) Kanibalisme

segments.tr: - (d) Populasi siang hari

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Trade area** — the geographic zone a store draws its customers from, usually divided into primary, secondary, and tertiary rings.
segments.tr: - **Wilayah perdagangan** — zona geografis tempat toko menarik pelanggannya, biasanya dibagi menjadi cincin utama, sekunder, dan tersier.

segments.src: - **Gravity model (Huff model)** — a method estimating the probability a shopper chooses a given store, where attraction rises with store size and falls with travel time.
segments.tr: - **Model gravitasi (Model Huff)** — metode memperkirakan kemungkinan pembeli memilih toko tertentu, di mana daya tarik meningkat dengan ukuran toko dan jatuh dengan waktu perjalanan.

segments.src: - **Anchor tenant** — the large, traffic-generating store (often a supermarket or big box) that a shopping center is built around; it typically pays lower rent per square foot in exchange for the traffic it brings.
segments.tr: - **Penyewa jangkar** — toko besar yang menghasilkan lalu lintas (sering supermarket atau kotak besar) yang dibangun di sekitarnya pusat perbelanjaan; biasanya membayar sewa lebih rendah per kaki persegi sebagai imbalan lalu lintas yang dibawanya.

segments.src: - **Co-tenancy clause** — a lease provision letting a small tenant reduce rent or exit if the anchor or a set share of the center goes vacant.
segments.tr: - **Klausul co-tenancy** — ketentuan sewa yang memungkinkan penyewa kecil mengurangi sewa atau keluar jika jangkar atau bagian tertentu dari pusat menjadi kosong.

segments.src: - **Cannibalization** — the share of a new store's sales taken from the retailer's own existing nearby locations rather than from competitors.
segments.tr: - **Kanibalisme** — pangsa penjualan toko baru yang diambil dari lokasi terdekat yang sudah ada dari pengecer itu sendiri daripada dari pesaing.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** In a gravity model, attraction is proportional to size and inversely related to distance or travel time raised to some exponent, so longer travel time means weaker pull.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **Q1 — (b).** Dalam model gravitasi, daya tarik sebanding dengan ukuran dan berbanding terbalik dengan jarak atau waktu perjalanan yang dipangkatkan ke beberapa eksponen, jadi waktu perjalanan yang lebih lama berarti tarikan yang lebih lemah.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** The anchor generally pays the *lowest* rent per square foot in the center, because its role is to generate the traffic the inline tenants depend on; those small shops pay a premium for that spillover.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (salah).** Jangkar umumnya membayar *sewa terendah* per kaki persegi di pusat, karena perannya adalah menghasilkan lalu lintas yang bergantung pada penyewa inline; toko-toko kecil itu membayar premi untuk tumpahan itu.

segments.src: **Q3 — (c) Cannibalization.** When trade areas overlap, part of the new store's revenue is transferred from an existing location rather than newly created — which is why site analysis models net incremental sales, not just gross sales at the new site.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — (c) Kanibalisme.** Ketika wilayah perdagangan tumpang tindih, bagian dari pendapatan toko baru ditransfer dari lokasi yang sudah ada daripada yang baru dibuat — itulah mengapa model analisis situs penjualan inkremental bersih, bukan hanya penjualan kotor di situs baru.*

segments.src: - **Traffic** — vehicle counts (published by state DOTs as annual average daily traffic, or AADT) and foot traffic. But raw volume isn't enough. Cars doing 55 mph past a median-divided highway can't turn left into your parking lot.
segments.tr: - **トラフィック** — 車両数（州の道路局により年間平均日交通量、またはAADTとして公開）と歩行者数。しかし、単純な数字だけでは不十分です。中央分離帯のある高速道路を時速55マイルで通過する車は、あなたの駐車場に左折することはできません。

segments.src: - **Accessibility** — curb cuts, signal lights, left-turn access, parking ratio (commonly around 4–5 spaces per 1,000 sq ft for shopping centers), and how easy it is to get *out* as well as in.
segments.tr: - **アクセシビリティ** — 縁石の切り込み、信号機、左折アクセス、駐車台数比率（ショッピングセンターでは通常1,000平方フィートあたり4～5台程度）、および「出る」のと同じくらい「入る」のがどれだけ簡単かどうか。

segments.src: - **Visibility** — sightlines from the road, signage rights, and how far ahead a driver can spot you.
segments.tr: - **可視性** — 道路からの視認性、標識の掲示権、運転手があなたをどれだけ遠くから発見できるか。

segments.src: - **Trade area demographics** — population, household income, age mix, and daytime population (the workers who show up 9-to-5 but sleep elsewhere).
segments.tr: - **商圏デモグラフィクス** — 人口、世帯収入、年齢構成、昼間人口（9時から5時に現れるが他の場所で眠る労働者）。

segments.src: - **Competition and co-tenancy** — nearby stores that steal your customers versus ones that deliver them. A nail salon wants to be next to a grocery anchor. A furniture store is happy next to another furniture store, because shoppers comparison-shop big-ticket items.
segments.tr: - **競争と共同テナント関係** — あなたの顧客を奪う近隣店舗対あなたに顧客をもたらす店舗。ネイルサロンは食料品アンカーの隣にいたいと考えています。家具店は別の家具店の隣にいることを喜んでいます。買い物客は高額商品を比較購入するからです。

segments.src: - **Cost and terms** — base rent per square foot per year, CAM (common area maintenance) charges, percentage rent, lease length, and any exclusivity or co-tenancy clauses.
segments.tr: - **コストと条件** — 年間1平方フィートあたりの基本賃料、CAM（共有エリア維持）料金、パーセンテージ賃料、リース期間、および排他的条項または共同テナント条項。

segments.src: Who can actually reach it?** That's **trade area analysis**.
segments.tr: 実際に到達できるのは誰か？** これが**商圏分析**です。

segments.src: A trade area is the geographic zone a store draws customers from, usually split into three rings:
segments.tr: 商圏は、店舗が顧客を引き付ける地理的ゾーンで、通常3つのリングに分かれています：

segments.src: - **Primary** — roughly 50–70% of customers, closest in
segments.tr: - **第1次圏** — 顧客の約50～70%、最も近い

segments.src: - **Secondary** — the next 20–30%
- **Tertiary** — the scattered remainder, including people passing through
segments.tr: - **第3次圏** — 散在した残り、通過する人を含む

segments.src: Practitioners rarely draw simple circles anymore.
segments.tr: 実務家はもはや単純な円を描くことはほとんどありません。

segments.src: They use **drive-time polygons** (a 5-, 10-, and 15-minute drive radius, which bends around rivers, highways, and dead ends) and, increasingly, anonymized mobile-location data showing where customers actually came from.
segments.tr: 彼らは**ドライブタイムポリゴン**（5分、10分、15分のドライブ半径で、川、高速道路、行き止まりを迂回する）を使用し、ますます匿名化されたモバイル位置データを使用して、顧客が実際にどこから来たかを示しています。

segments.src: The classic analytical tool is the **gravity model**.
segments.tr: 古典的な分析ツールは**重力モデル**です。

segments.src: The intuition is borrowed from physics: a store's pull grows with its size and shrinks with the distance (or travel time) shoppers must cover.
segments.tr: その直感は物理学から借りています。店舗の引力はそのサイズとともに大きくなり、買い物客が移動する必要がある距離（または移動時間）とともに小さくなります。

segments.src: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k
segments.tr: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k

segments.src: The Huff model formalizes this — it estimates the *probability* a given household shops at Store A rather than Store B, which is more useful than a hard boundary line, because real trade areas are fuzzy and overlapping.
segments.tr: ハフモデルはこれを形式化しています。特定の家庭がストアBではなくストアAで買い物をする*確率*を推定します。これは固い境界線よりも有用です。実際の商圏はあいまいで重複しているからです。

segments.src: A related check is **cannibalization**: if your new store's trade area overlaps an existing one you already own, part of your "new" sales is just sales moving across town.
segments.tr: 関連するチェックは**カニバリゼーション**です。新しい店舗の商圏が既存の店舗と重なる場合、「新しい」売上の一部は単に町を越えて移動する売上です。

segments.src: What kind of site is it?** Location types come with built-in trade-offs:
segments.tr: どのような種類のサイトか？** 立地タイプはトレードオフを内蔵しています：

segments.src: - **Unplanned / freestanding** — a standalone building, often a pad or outparcel at the edge of a shopping center lot. Cheap per square foot, great parking, full signage control, but no neighbor pulling traffic for you. Works for destination brands (Walgreens, a drive-thru quick-service restaurant).
segments.tr: - **計画外/独立型** — スタンドアロンの建物で、ショッピングセンターロットの端にあるパッドまたはアウトパーセルが多い。1平方フィートあたり安い、駐車が素晴らしい、標識の完全なコントロール、しかしあなたのためにトラフィックを引く隣人がいない。目的地ブランド（Walgreens、ドライブスルー型ファストサービスレストラン）に有効です。

segments.src: - **Central business district (CBD)** — downtown. High daytime population, high rent, limited parking, weekend traffic that can fall off a cliff in office-heavy districts.
segments.tr: - **中央ビジネス地区（CBD）** — ダウンタウン。高い昼間人口、高い賃料、限定的な駐車、オフィス密集地区で激減する可能性のある週末交通。

segments.src: - **Strip / neighborhood center** — a line of stores with surface parking, usually anchored by a supermarket or a drugstore. Built for convenience and errand trips.
segments.tr: - **ストリップ/近隣センター** — 地表駐車を備えた店舗の列、通常はスーパーマーケットまたはドラッグストアを中心に。利便性と買い物かごの移動のために構築されています。

segments.src: - **Power center** — a cluster of big-box category killers (home improvement, pet supply, off-price apparel). Draws from a wide radius.
segments.tr: - **パワーセンター** — ビッグボックスカテゴリーキラー（ホーム改善、ペット用品、割引衣料品）のクラスター。広い半径から引き付けます。

segments.src: - **Enclosed regional mall** — big trade area, high traffic, high rent, strict operating rules and long leases.
segments.tr: - **囲まれた地域モール** — 大きな商圏、高交通量、高賃料、厳格な運営規則と長期リース。

segments.src: - **Lifestyle center** — open-air, upscale, restaurant-heavy; sells atmosphere and dwell time.
segments.tr: - **ライフスタイルセンター** — オープンエア、高級、レストランが多い。雰囲気と滞在時間を販売しています。

segments.src: - **Airports, campuses, transit hubs** — captive audiences, premium pricing, brutal rent and operating restrictions.
segments.tr: - **空港、キャンパス、交通ハブ** — 捕虜にされた観客、プレミアム価格、厳しい賃料と運営制限。

segments.src: The right answer depends entirely on format.
segments.tr: 正しい答えは完全にフォーマットに依存します。

segments.src: A convenience store needs a right-turn-in on the evening commute side of the road.
segments.tr: コンビニエンスストアは夕方の通勤側の道路上で右折入場を必要とします。

segments.src: A destination retailer like IKEA can sit by a highway interchange 25 minutes away and still fill the lot, because people plan the trip.
segments.tr: IKEAのような目的地小売業者は25分離れた高速道路インターチェンジの近くに座ることができ、それでも多くの人を引き付けることができます。人々が旅行を計画するからです。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks and a Costco in the same American suburb.
segments.tr: 同じアメリカの郊外にあるスターバックスとコストコを考えてみてください。

segments.src: The Starbucks sits on the *morning* side of a busy arterial — the inbound-commute side — with a right-turn-in entrance and a drive-thru wrapping the building.
segments.tr: スターバックスは忙しい幹線道路の*朝*側（通勤ルート側）に位置し、右折入場と建物をラップするドライブスルーがあります。

segments.src: Its primary trade area may be only a mile or two wide.
segments.tr: その第1次商圏は幅1～2マイル程度かもしれません。

segments.src: Nobody plans a 20-minute drive for a latte, so it lives on interception: catching a trip already in progress.
segments.tr: ラテのために20分のドライブを計画する人はいないので、それは傍受に住んでいます。既に進行中の旅をつかむ。

segments.src: That's why you'll see two Starbucks locations facing each other across the same road.
segments.tr: そのため、同じ道路を挟んで向かい合う2つのスターバックスの場所が見えます。

segments.src: They're not competing so much as covering opposite commute directions, and the company accepts a bit of cannibalization to own both flows.
segments.tr: 彼らはそれほど競争しているのではなく、反対の通勤方向をカバーしており、同社は両方のフローを所有するためにある程度のカニバリゼーションを受け入れています。

segments.src: Costco plays the opposite game.
segments.tr: コストコは反対のゲームをしています。

segments.src: There's one per region, usually near a freeway interchange with a huge lot and a gas station out front.
segments.tr: 地域ごとに1つあり、通常は広大なロットと前面ガソリンスタンドを持つフリーウェイインターチェンジの近くにあります。

segments.src: People will drive 25 minutes and load a cart with $250 of goods.
segments.tr: 人々は25分運転し、カートに$250相当の商品を積み込みます。

segments.src: Its trade area is measured in a 15-minute-plus drive time, not blocks.
segments.tr: その商圏は15分以上のドライブタイムで測定され、ブロック単位ではありません。

segments.src: The gravity model explains both: Costco's enormous size overcomes distance decay, while Starbucks' small size means it must live very close to its customer.
segments.tr: 重力モデルはその両方を説明しています。コストコの莫大なサイズは距離減衰を克服し、スターバックスの小さなサイズは顧客の非常に近くに住む必要があることを意味しています。

segments.src: Now look at the strip mall nearby.
segments.tr: 今は近くのストリップモールを見てください。

segments.src: The grocery anchor probably pays $8–$15 per square foot in annual base rent, while the small inline shops next to it might pay $30–$45, plus $5–$10 in CAM.
segments.tr: 食料品アンカーは年間1平方フィートあたり$8～$15の基本賃料を支払う可能性がありますが、その隣の小さなインラインショップは$30～$45、プラスCAMで$5～$10を支払う可能性があります。

segments.src: The anchor pays less because it *generates* the traffic everyone else feeds on.
segments.tr: アンカーはより少なく支払います。なぜなら、それは他のすべてが供給するトラフィックを*生成*するからです。

segments.src: And many small-shop leases include a **co-tenancy clause**: if the anchor goes dark, the small tenant can cut rent or walk.
segments.tr: そして、多くの小売店リースには**共同テナント条項**が含まれています。アンカーが消えた場合、小さなテナントは賃料を削減するか去ることができます。

segments.src: That clause exists precisely because their location value came from the neighbor, not the address.
segments.tr: その条項が存在するのは、彼らのロケーション価値がアドレスではなく隣人から来たからです。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行の要約

segments.src: 1. Site selection weighs traffic, accessibility, visibility, trade-area demographics, competition and co-tenancy, and total occupancy cost — not just rent.
segments.tr: 1. サイト選択は、トラフィック、アクセシビリティ、可視性、商圏デモグラフィクス、競争と共同テナント関係、および総占有コストを考慮します。単なる賃料ではありません。

segments.src: 2. Trade area analysis defines who can realistically reach a store, using drive-time zones and gravity/Huff models that trade hard boundaries for probabilities, while watching for cannibalization of your own stores.
segments.tr: 2. 商圏分析は、ドライブタイムゾーンと重力/ハフモデルを使用して、実際に店舗に到達できるのは誰かを定義し、固い境界を確率と交換し、自社店舗のカニバリゼーションを監視します。

segments.src: 3. Location type — freestanding, CBD, strip center, power center, mall, lifestyle center, or captive venue — must match the store's format, because convenience retailers intercept trips while destination retailers can pull people across a whole metro.
segments.tr: 3. 立地タイプ（独立型、CBD、ストリップセンター、パワーセンター、モール、ライフスタイルセンター、または捕虜会場）は、店舗のフォーマットと一致する必要があります。利便性小売業者は旅をインターセプトし、目的地小売業者はメトロ全体で人を引き付けることができるからです。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自己クイズ

segments.src: **Q1.** In a gravity model of retail attraction, what happens to a store's pull as travel time increases, holding store size constant?
segments.tr: **Q1.** 小売引力の重力モデルで、店舗のサイズを一定に保ちながら移動時間が増加すると、店舗の引力はどうなりますか？

segments.src: - (a) It increases
segments.tr: - (a) 増加する

segments.src: - (b) It decreases
segments.tr: - (b) 減少する

segments.src: - (c) It stays the same
segments.tr: - (c) 同じままである

segments.src: - (d) It depends entirely on rent
segments.tr: - (d) それは完全に賃料に依存する

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — In a typical neighborhood shopping center, the grocery anchor usually pays a *higher* base rent per square foot than the small inline shops beside it.
segments.tr: **Q2.** ○/X — 典型的な近隣ショッピングセンターでは、食料品アンカーは通常、その隣の小さなインラインショップよりも1平方フィートあたり*高い*基本賃料を支払います。

segments.src: **Q3.** A retailer opens a second store four miles from its existing one and total company sales rise far less than the new store's own sales.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 小売業者は既存の店舗から4マイル離れた2番目の店舗を開き、総会社売上が新店舗自体の売上よりもはるかに少なく増加します。

segments.src: What is this most likely called?
segments.tr: これは最もおそらく何と呼ばれていますか？

segments.src: - (a) Co-tenancy
segments.tr: - (a) 共同テナント関係

segments.src: - (b) Percentage rent
segments.tr: - (b) パーセンテージ賃料

segments.src: - (c) Cannibalization
segments.tr: - (c) カニバリゼーション

segments.src: - (d) Daytime population
segments.tr: - (d) 昼間人口

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 本日の用語

segments.src: - **Trade area** — the geographic zone a store draws its customers from, usually divided into primary, secondary, and tertiary rings.
segments.tr: - **商圏** — 店舗が顧客を引き付ける地理的ゾーン、通常は第1次、第2次、第3次リングに分かれています。

segments.src: - **Gravity model (Huff model)** — a method estimating the probability a shopper chooses a given store, where attraction rises with store size and falls with travel time.
segments.tr: - **重力モデル（ハフモデル）** — 買い物客が特定の店舗を選ぶ確率を推定する方法で、引力は店舗サイズとともに上昇し、移動時間とともに低下します。

segments.src: - **Anchor tenant** — the large, traffic-generating store (often a supermarket or big box) that a shopping center is built around; it typically pays lower rent per square foot in exchange for the traffic it brings.
segments.tr: - **アンカーテナント** — ショッピングセンターを中心に構築された大規模なトラフィック生成店舗（通常はスーパーマーケットまたはビッグボックス）。通常、持ってくるトラフィックと引き換えに1平方フィートあたり低い賃料を支払う。

segments.src: - **Co-tenancy clause** — a lease provision letting a small tenant reduce rent or exit if the anchor or a set share of the center goes vacant.
segments.tr: - **共同テナント条項** — アンカーまたはセンターの設定されたシェアが空き家になった場合、小さなテナントが賃料を削減または終了することを可能にするリース条項。

segments.src: - **Cannibalization** — the share of a new store's sales taken from the retailer's own existing nearby locations rather than from competitors.
segments.tr: - **カニバリゼーション** — 競合他社ではなく、小売業者自身の既存の近隣店舗から取られた新店舗の売上のシェア。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (b).** In a gravity model, attraction is proportional to size and inversely related to distance or travel time raised to some exponent, so longer travel time means weaker pull.
segments.tr: *答え: **Q1 — (b).** 重力モデルでは、引力はサイズに比例し、距離または移動時間のいくつかの指数に逆に関連しているため、より長い移動時間はより弱い引力を意味します。

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** The anchor generally pays the *lowest* rent per square foot in the center, because its role is to generate the traffic the inline tenants depend on; those small shops pay a premium for that spillover.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (偽).** アンカーは一般的にセンター内で1平方フィートあたり*最も低い*賃料を支払います。その役割はインラインテナントが依存するトラフィックを生成することだからです。小さなショップはそのスピルオーバーのためにプレミアムを支払う。

segments.src: **Q3 — (c) Cannibalization.** When trade areas overlap, part of the new store's revenue is transferred from an existing location rather than newly created — which is why site analysis models net incremental sales, not just gross sales at the new site.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — (c) カニバリゼーション。** 商圏が重なる場合、新店舗の収益の一部は新しく作成されたのではなく既存の場所から転送されます。これがサイト分析モデルが新店舗での総売上だけでなく、正味増分売上をモデル化する理由です。*

de.title: [Retailing 101 #11] Warum die eine Ecke Geld druckt und der nächste Block verblasst

segments.src: > Retail real estate isn't about finding a "good spot" — it's about matching a specific store format to the specific pool of people who can realistically reach it.
segments.tr: > Immobilien im Einzelhandel geht es nicht darum, einen "guten Platz" zu finden — es geht darum, ein bestimmtes Geschäftsformat mit der bestimmten Gruppe von Menschen zu kombinieren, die es realistisch erreichen können.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Heutiges Konzept

segments.src: There's an old line in retail: the three things that matter are location, location, and location.
segments.tr: Es gibt einen alten Spruch im Einzelhandel: die drei Dinge, die zählen, sind Standort, Standort und Standort.

segments.src: It's a cliché, but it survives because store location is one of the few decisions you can't undo cheaply.
segments.tr: Es ist ein Klischee, aber es hält sich, weil der Standort eines Geschäfts eine der wenigen Entscheidungen ist, die man nicht günstig rückgängig machen kann.

segments.src: You can re-merchandise a shelf on Tuesday.
segments.tr: Sie können ein Regal am Dienstag neu bestücken.

segments.src: You can drop prices tonight.
segments.tr: Sie können die Preise heute Abend senken.

segments.src: You cannot move a 30,000-square-foot building with a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: Sie können kein 30.000 Quadratmeter großes Gebäude mit einem 15-jährigen Mietvertrag verschieben.

segments.src: Location strategy breaks into three questions that get asked in order.
segments.tr: Die Standortstrategie gliedert sich in drei Fragen, die der Reihe nach gestellt werden.

segments.src: What factors make a site work?** Retailers evaluate sites on a handful of measurable things:
segments.tr: Welche Faktoren machen einen Standort wertvoll?** Einzelhändler evaluieren Standorte anhand einer Handvoll messbarer Dinge:

segments.src: - **Traffic** — vehicle counts (published by state DOTs as annual average daily traffic, or AADT) and foot traffic. But raw volume isn't enough. Cars doing 55 mph past a median-divided highway can't turn left into your parking lot.
segments.tr: - **Verkehr** — Fahrzeugzählungen (von staatlichen Verkehrsministerien als durchschnittlicher täglicher Verkehr oder AADT veröffentlicht) und Fußverkehr. Aber das reine Volumen reicht nicht. Autos, die mit 55 mph an einer Mitteltrennung vorbeifahren, können nicht links in Ihren Parkplatz abbiegen.

segments.src: - **Accessibility** — curb cuts, signal lights, left-turn access, parking ratio (commonly around 4–5 spaces per 1,000 sq ft for shopping centers), and how easy it is to get *out* as well as in.
segments.tr: - **Erreichbarkeit** — Bordsteine, Ampeln, Linksabbiegezugang, Parkplatzquote (üblicherweise etwa 4–5 Plätze pro 1.000 Quadratmeter für Einkaufszentren) und wie leicht es ist, zu fahren und auch wieder herauszukommen.

segments.src: - **Visibility** — sightlines from the road, signage rights, and how far ahead a driver can spot you.
segments.tr: - **Sichtbarkeit** — Sichtlinien von der Straße, Beschilderungsrechte und wie weit im Voraus ein Fahrer Sie erkennen kann.

segments.src: - **Trade area demographics** — population, household income, age mix, and daytime population (the workers who show up 9-to-5 but sleep elsewhere).
segments.tr: - **Marktgebiet-Demografie** — Bevölkerung, Haushaltseinkommen, Altersstruktur und Tagsüber-Bevölkerung (die Arbeiter, die 9-to-5 kommen, aber woanders schlafen).

segments.src: - **Competition and co-tenancy** — nearby stores that steal your customers versus ones that deliver them. A nail salon wants to be next to a grocery anchor. A furniture store is happy next to another furniture store, because shoppers comparison-shop big-ticket items.
segments.tr: - **Wettbewerb und Co-Mieter** — benachbarte Geschäfte, die Ihre Kunden abziehen, gegenüber solchen, die sie zu Ihnen bringen. Ein Nagelstudio möchte neben einem Lebensmittel-Anker sein. Ein Möbelgeschäft ist glücklich neben einem anderen Möbelgeschäft, weil Käufer bei großen Anschaffungen vergleichen.

segments.src: - **Cost and terms** — base rent per square foot per year, CAM (common area maintenance) charges, percentage rent, lease length, and any exclusivity or co-tenancy clauses.
segments.tr: - **Kosten und Bedingungen** — Grundmiete pro Quadratmeter pro Jahr, Nebenkosten (common area maintenance), Prozentmiete, Mietdauer und alle Ausschließlichkeits- oder Co-Mieter-Klauseln.

segments.src: Who can actually reach it?** That's **trade area analysis**.
segments.tr: Wer kann es wirklich erreichen?** Das ist **Marktgebiet-Analyse**.

segments.src: A trade area is the geographic zone a store draws customers from, usually split into three rings:
segments.tr: Ein Marktgebiet ist die geografische Zone, aus der ein Geschäft Kunden anzieht, üblicherweise in drei Ringe unterteilt:

segments.src: - **Primary** — roughly 50–70% of customers, closest in
segments.tr: - **Primär** — ungefähr 50–70% der Kunden, am nächsten gelegen

segments.src: - **Secondary** — the next 20–30%
segments.tr: - **Sekundär** — die nächsten 20–30%

segments.src: - **Tertiary** — the scattered remainder, including people passing through
segments.tr: - **Tertiär** — der zerstreute Rest, einschließlich Personen, die vorbeifahren

segments.src: Practitioners rarely draw simple circles anymore.
segments.tr: Praktiker zeichnen selten einfache Kreise.

segments.src: They use **drive-time polygons** (a 5-, 10-, and 15-minute drive radius, which bends around rivers, highways, and dead ends) and, increasingly, anonymized mobile-location data showing where customers actually came from.
segments.tr: Sie verwenden **Fahrtzeit-Polygone** (ein 5-, 10- und 15-Minuten-Fahrtzeit-Radius, der sich um Flüsse, Autobahnen und Sackgassen biegt) und zunehmend anonymisierte Mobiltelefonstandortdaten, die zeigen, woher Kunden wirklich kamen.

segments.src: The classic analytical tool is the **gravity model**.
segments.tr: Das klassische Analysetool ist das **Gravitationsmodell**.

segments.src: The intuition is borrowed from physics: a store's pull grows with its size and shrinks with the distance (or travel time) shoppers must cover.
segments.tr: Die Intuition ist aus der Physik entlehnt: Die Anziehungskraft eines Geschäfts wächst mit seiner Größe und schrumpft mit der Entfernung (oder Fahrzeit), die Käufer zurücklegen müssen.

segments.src: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k
segments.tr: attraction ≈ store size ÷ (travel time)^k

segments.src: The Huff model formalizes this — it estimates the *probability* a given household shops at Store A rather than Store B, which is more useful than a hard boundary line, because real trade areas are fuzzy and overlapping.
segments.tr: Das Huff-Modell formalisiert dies — es schätzt die *Wahrscheinlichkeit*, dass ein bestimmter Haushalt in Geschäft A statt Geschäft B einkauft, was nützlicher ist als eine harte Grenzlinie, denn echte Marktgebiete sind verschwommen und überlappend.

segments.src: A related check is **cannibalization**: if your new store's trade area overlaps an existing one you already own, part of your "new" sales is just sales moving across town.
segments.tr: Eine verwandte Überprüfung ist **Kannibalisierung**: Wenn das Marktgebiet Ihres neuen Geschäfts ein bestehendes überlappt, das Sie bereits besitzen, ist ein Teil Ihres "neuen" Umsatzes einfach nur Umsatz, der sich über die Stadt verlagert.

segments.src: What kind of site is it?** Location types come with built-in trade-offs:
segments.tr: Was für ein Standort ist das?** Standorttypen haben eingebaute Kompromisse:

segments.src: - **Unplanned / freestanding** — a standalone building, often a pad or outparcel at the edge of a shopping center lot. Cheap per square foot, great parking, full signage control, but no neighbor pulling traffic for you. Works for destination brands (Walgreens, a drive-thru quick-service restaurant).
segments.tr: - **Ungeplant / freistehendes Gebäude** — ein eigenständiges Gebäude, oft ein Grundstück oder Außenparzelle am Rande eines Einkaufszentrums. Günstig pro Quadratmeter, großartige Parkplätze, volle Kontrolle über Beschilderung, aber kein Nachbar zieht Verkehr für Sie. Funktioniert für Zielgeschäfte (Walgreens, ein Drive-in-Restaurant).

segments.src: - **Central business district (CBD)** — downtown. High daytime population, high rent, limited parking, weekend traffic that can fall off a cliff in office-heavy districts.
segments.tr: - **Zentraler Geschäftsbezirk (CBD)** — Innenstadt. Hohe Tagsüber-Bevölkerung, hohe Miete, begrenzte Parkplätze, Wochenendverkehr, der in bürodominierten Bezirken einbrechen kann.

segments.src: - **Strip / neighborhood center** — a line of stores with surface parking, usually anchored by a supermarket or a drugstore. Built for convenience and errand trips.
segments.tr: - **Ladenzeile / Nachbarschafts-Center** — eine Reihe von Geschäften mit Oberflächenparkplatz, üblicherweise verankert durch einen Supermarkt oder eine Drogerie. Gebaut für Bequemlichkeit und Besorgungen.

segments.src: - **Power center** — a cluster of big-box category killers (home improvement, pet supply, off-price apparel). Draws from a wide radius.
segments.tr: - **Handelscenter** — eine Ansammlung von großflächigen Kategorie-Killern (Heimwerkermarkt, Tierbedarf, Outlet-Kleidung). Zieht aus einem weiten Radius an.

segments.src: - **Enclosed regional mall** — big trade area, high traffic, high rent, strict operating rules and long leases.
segments.tr: - **Einkaufszentrum (überdacht)** — großes Marktgebiet, hoher Verkehr, hohe Miete, strenge Betriebsregeln und lange Mietverträge.

segments.src: - **Lifestyle center** — open-air, upscale, restaurant-heavy; sells atmosphere and dwell time.
segments.tr: - **Lifestyle-Center** — Freiluft, gehobener Standard, restaurantlastig; verkauft Atmosphäre und Verweilzeit.

segments.src: - **Airports, campuses, transit hubs** — captive audiences, premium pricing, brutal rent and operating restrictions.
segments.tr: - **Flughäfen, Campusse, Verkehrsknotenpunkte** — gefangenes Publikum, Premium-Preisgestaltung, brutale Miete und Betriebsbeschränkungen.

segments.src: The right answer depends entirely on format.
segments.tr: Die richtige Antwort hängt ganz vom Format ab.

segments.src: A convenience store needs a right-turn-in on the evening commute side of the road.
segments.tr: Ein Convenience-Store braucht einen Rechtsabbiegerzugang auf der Seite des Feierabendverkehrs.

segments.src: A destination retailer like IKEA can sit by a highway interchange 25 minutes away and still fill the lot, because people plan the trip.
segments.tr: Ein Zielgeschäft wie IKEA kann neben einer Autobahnausfahrt 25 Minuten weg sitzen und den Parkplatz immer noch füllen, weil Menschen den Ausflug planen.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Think about a Starbucks and a Costco in the same American suburb.
segments.tr: Denken Sie an einen Starbucks und einen Costco in demselben amerikanischen Vorort.

segments.src: The Starbucks sits on the *morning* side of a busy arterial — the inbound-commute side — with a right-turn-in entrance and a drive-thru wrapping the building.
segments.tr: Der Starbucks sitzt auf der *Morgen*-Seite einer belebten Hauptstraße — der Seite des Pendelverkehrs in die Stadt — mit einem Rechtsabbiegerzugang und einem Drive-in-Schalter, der das Gebäude umgibt.

segments.src: Its primary trade area may be only a mile or two wide.
segments.tr: Sein primäres Marktgebiet kann nur eine bis zwei Meilen breit sein.

segments.src: Nobody plans a 20-minute drive for a latte, so it lives on interception: catching a trip already in progress.
segments.tr: Niemand plant eine 20-minütige Fahrt für einen Latte, also lebt es von Abfangen: Ich fange einen bereits laufenden Trip auf.

segments.src: That's why you'll see two Starbucks locations facing each other across the same road.
segments.tr: Deshalb sehen Sie oft zwei Starbucks-Standorte, die sich über die gleiche Straße ansehen.

segments.src: They're not competing so much as covering opposite commute directions, and the company accepts a bit of cannibalization to own both flows.
segments.tr: Sie konkurrieren nicht so sehr, sondern decken entgegengesetzte Pendelrichtungen ab, und das Unternehmen akzeptiert ein wenig Kannibalisierung, um beide Ströme zu besitzen.

segments.src: Costco plays the opposite game.
segments.tr: Costco spielt das gegensätzliche Spiel.

segments.src: There's one per region, usually near a freeway interchange with a huge lot and a gas station out front.
segments.tr: Es gibt einen pro Region, üblicherweise in der Nähe einer Autobahnausfahrt mit einem riesigen Parkplatz und einer Tankstelle davor.

segments.src: People will drive 25 minutes and load a cart with $250 of goods.
segments.tr: Leute werden 25 Minuten fahren und einen Wagen mit 250 Dollar Waren laden.

segments.src: Its trade area is measured in a 15-minute-plus drive time, not blocks.
segments.tr: Sein Marktgebiet wird in einer 15-Minuten-Plus-Fahrtzeit gemessen, nicht in Blöcken.

segments.src: The gravity model explains both: Costco's enormous size overcomes distance decay, while Starbucks' small size means it must live very close to its customer.
segments.tr: Das Gravitationsmodell erklärt beide: Costcos enorme Größe überwindet Distanzzerfall, während Starbucks' kleine Größe bedeutet, dass es sehr nah bei seinen Kunden leben muss.

segments.src: Now look at the strip mall nearby.
segments.tr: Schauen Sie sich jetzt die Ladenzeile in der Nähe an.

segments.src: The grocery anchor probably pays $8–$15 per square foot in annual base rent, while the small inline shops next to it might pay $30–$45, plus $5–$10 in CAM.
segments.tr: Der Lebensmittel-Anker zahlt wahrscheinlich 8–15 Dollar pro Quadratmeter in jährlicher Grundmiete, während die kleinen Inline-Geschäfte daneben 30–45 Dollar zahlen könnten, plus 5–10 Dollar in Nebenkosten.

segments.src: The anchor pays less because it *generates* the traffic everyone else feeds on.
segments.tr: Der Anker zahlt weniger, weil er *erzeugt* den Verkehr, von dem alle anderen leben.

segments.src: And many small-shop leases include a **co-tenancy clause**: if the anchor goes dark, the small tenant can cut rent or walk.
segments.tr: Und viele Mietverträge für kleine Geschäfte enthalten eine **Co-Mieter-Klausel**: Wenn der Anker dunkel wird, kann der kleine Mieter die Miete kürzen oder gehen.

segments.src: That clause exists precisely because their location value came from the neighbor, not the address.
segments.tr: Diese Klausel existiert genau deshalb, weil ihr Standortwert vom Nachbarn kam, nicht von der Adresse.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Drei-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. Site selection weighs traffic, accessibility, visibility, trade-area demographics, competition and co-tenancy, and total occupancy cost — not just rent.
segments.tr: 1. Die Standortauswahl wiegt Verkehr, Erreichbarkeit, Sichtbarkeit, Marktgebiet-Demografie, Wettbewerb und Co-Mieter sowie Gesamtbetriebskosten — nicht nur Miete.

segments.src: 2. Trade area analysis defines who can realistically reach a store, using drive-time zones and gravity/Huff models that trade hard boundaries for probabilities, while watching for cannibalization of your own stores.
segments.tr: 2. Die Marktgebiet-Analyse definiert, wer einen Laden realistisch erreichen kann, wobei Fahrtzeit-Zonen und Gravitationsmodelle verwendet werden, die harte Grenzen gegen Wahrscheinlichkeiten tauschen, während man auf Kannibalisierung Ihrer eigenen Geschäfte achtet.

segments.src: 3. Location type — freestanding, CBD, strip center, power center, mall, lifestyle center, or captive venue — must match the store's format, because convenience retailers intercept trips while destination retailers can pull people across a whole metro.
segments.tr: 3. Der Standorttyp — freistehendes Gebäude, CBD, Ladenzeile, Handelscenter, Einkaufszentrum, Lifestyle-Center oder gefangener Ort — muss dem Geschäftsformat entsprechen, weil Convenience-Einzelhändler Trips abfangen, während Zielgeschäfte Menschen über eine ganze Metropole ziehen können.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.tr: **F1.** In einem Gravitationsmodell der Einzelhandelsanziehung, was passiert mit der Anziehungskraft eines Geschäfts, wenn die Fahrtzeit zunimmt, während die Geschäftsgröße konstant bleibt?
